### Renamed

- `--ds-vert` → `--ds-vert` — Value corrected #89fc79 -> #53ff64. The 0.11 hex was eye-dropped from the charter PNG on the belief that the swatch label was a typo; the label was right. Name unchanged — re-check any hard-coded copy of the old hex. (batch 0.3)
- `--ds-accent (in charts, sparkline, bar-chart series)` → `--ds-chart-1` — Data series no longer read the themeable accent. Visually identical at the default theme (--ds-chart-1 is #ff2a00); a theme that overrode --ds-accent to recolour its charts must now override --ds-chart-*. (batch 0.3)
- `Wordmark ({ name, sub })` → `Wordmark ({ variant, label, name, sub })` — The geometric construction 0.x drew — a circle, a square and a diagonal line, the brand's three elements as primitives — is replaced by the produced lockups, as two `currentColor` variants: `horizontal` (the full name) and `square` (the monogram). `name` and `sub` are unchanged and still render `.ds-wordmark__name` / `__sub`, but they no longer default: a bare <Wordmark /> is now the lockup alone, where it used to print the word "Diametral". A name beside the mark wants variant="square" — the horizontal lockup already spells it. `.ds-wordmark__mark` still styles a hand-written svg; the React binding emits none. `assets/logo/diametral-mark.svg` still holds the geometric mark and has not been re-cut to match. (batch 3)
- `.ds-wordmark, .ds-wordmark__mark, .ds-wordmark__name, .ds-wordmark__sub (in app-bar.css)` → `.ds-wordmark, .ds-wordmark__mark, .ds-wordmark__name, .ds-wordmark__sub (in wordmark.css)` — File move only, no rename and no visual change — the four rules left app-bar.css for the new wordmark.css when the real lockup landed. Anyone importing css/diametral.css is unaffected; only a consumer cherry-picking css/components/app-bar.css has to add css/components/wordmark.css. (batch 3)
- `.ds-button-group (in button-extras.css)` → `.ds-button-group (in button-group.css)` — Replaced wholesale, same name. The seam no longer overlaps members with margin-left: -1px; it removes the losing border with border-inline-start-width, which is identical in LTR and correct in RTL. Every selector matches both the new parts' data-slot and .ds-button/.ds-input/.ds-select, so existing markup keeps joining. New: [data-orientation="vertical"], .ds-button-group-text and .ds-button-group-separator. (batch 3)
- `IconButton ({ size: "sm" | "lg" })` → `IconButton ({ size: "icon" | "icon-xs" | "icon-sm" | "icon-lg" | "xs" | "sm" | "lg" })` — Additive, not a rename: `sm` and `lg` keep working, and `icon-` is simply stripped, so the source's four square spellings resolve onto the same boxes. `icon-xs` (24px, .ds-button--xs) is new. `label` was already required on both sides — the ledger's "incumbent is a class-applier" premise does not hold here, the same way batch-plan §1.1 found for stat-card. Moved from react/components/ButtonExtras.tsx to react/components/icon-button.tsx; the barrel import is unchanged. (batch 3)
- `GaugeChart, GaugeChartProps, GaugeChartThreshold` → `Gauge, GaugeThreshold` — Renamed with the absorption; every prop survives (`value`, `max`, `size`, `thickness`, `label`, `color`, `thresholds`, `format`) and the props interface is gone in favour of the inline type, the way every absorbed component declares its props. A find-and-replace of the symbol is the whole migration. (batch 4)
- `LineChart ({ series, data, labels, width, height })` → `LineChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey })` — Recharts replaced the hand-rolled SVG, so a series is named and coloured once in `config` — one entry per key in each `data` row — and the rows are objects rather than parallel arrays. `labels` becomes `xAxisKey`, the row field holding them; `width`/`height` become the container's box (`.ds-chart-container--plot`, retuned with `--ds-chart-height`). `grid` and `dots` are unchanged. Same for AreaChart, which additionally gains `stacked`. (batch 4)
- `AreaChart ({ series, data, labels, width, height })` → `AreaChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey, stacked })` — See LineChart. `stacked` is new: two areas drawn over each other are usually meant to sum. (batch 4)
- `BarChart ({ data: BarChartDatum[] })` → `BarChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey, statusKey, max, horizontal, stacked })` — 0.11 took one array of `{ label, value, status }`; the rows are now recharts rows and the measure is a `config` key. `status` moves from the datum to `statusKey`, a row field naming the tone, and all six 0.11 tones survive (success, warning, danger, critical, neutral, info) — the source's own map had only four. `horizontal` and `max` keep their 0.11 names and meaning. BarChartDatum is gone. (batch 4)
- `StackedBar ({ segments, showLegend })` → `StackedBar ({ config, data, labelKey, showLegend })` — Still the share chart: each row is normalised to its own total. `segments` and their colours become `config`; the row label becomes `labelKey`. For raw magnitudes rather than shares, use BarChart with `stacked`. (batch 4)
- `PieChart ({ data, color, legend, size })` → `PieChart ({ config, data, valueKey, nameKey, legend })` — `valueKey`/`nameKey` name the row fields; a slice's colour is a `config` entry keyed by its name, which is also how the tooltip and legend find its label. `size` becomes the container's square box — retune it with `--ds-chart-height`. (batch 4)
- `DonutChart ({ data, centerLabel, thickness, legend, size })` → `DonutChart ({ config, data, valueKey, nameKey, centerLabel, centerCaption, thickness, legend })` — See PieChart. `thickness` is now a percentage of the chart radius, not px, because the container is responsive and a px ring would not scale with it. `centerCaption` is new: the uppercase line under the figure, in the register Gauge uses. (batch 4)
- `Sparkline (flat series drawn along the floor)` → `Sparkline (flat series pinned to the middle)` — Props are unchanged. The one behavioural change is a defect fix: 0.11 divided by a `|| 1` span, so a flat series — or a single point — drew along the bottom of the box and read as a minimum it was not. It now pins to the vertical middle. (batch 4)
- `.ds-chart, .ds-chart__svg, .ds-chart__grid, .ds-chart__axis` → `.ds-chart-container` — The chart merge: charts.css and bar-chart.css were deleted and the source's chart.css landed in their place. The wrapper survives as .ds-chart-container; the svg, gridlines and axis labels do not, because recharts generates those nodes itself and they cannot carry a ds-* class. chart.css restyles them through `.ds-chart-container .recharts-*` descendant rules instead. A hand-written static chart has no replacement markup — the axis charts are React-only from 1.0.0-beta.4 on. `.ds-sparkline` and `.ds-gauge` are the two that stay library-free. (batch 4)
- `.ds-chart-legend, .ds-chart-legend__item, .ds-chart-legend__swatch` → `.ds-chart-legend-content, .ds-chart-legend-content-item, .ds-chart-legend-content-dot` — Rename only; the swatch is still a 10px square. `.ds-chart-legend__value` has no replacement — the source's legend carries a label, not a label plus a figure. (batch 4)
- `.ds-chart-legend__value` → _removed_ — Removed with the chart merge. Print the figure in the tooltip (`.ds-chart-tooltip-content-item-value`), or beside the chart as prose. (batch 4)
- `.ds-linechart, .ds-linechart__line, .ds-linechart__dot, .ds-areachart, .ds-areachart__line, .ds-areachart__area, .ds-areachart__dot` → _removed_ — Removed with the chart merge: the marks are recharts <path> nodes now, styled per series from `config` rather than by class. There is no static markup that reproduces them. (batch 4)
- `.ds-barchart, .ds-barchart--horizontal, .ds-barchart__col, .ds-barchart__track, .ds-barchart__bar, .ds-barchart__label, .ds-barchart__value` → _removed_ — Removed with the chart merge (bar-chart.css deleted). The CSS-flex bar chart — inline height/width percentages and `.is-success`-style tones on the bar — is replaced by recharts marks; the tone axis survives as BarChart's `statusKey`. (batch 4)
- `.ds-stackedbar, .ds-stackedbar__row, .ds-stackedbar__label, .ds-stackedbar__track, .ds-stackedbar__seg` → `.ds-stacked-bar-root` — Only the root survives, and its job is now the box: full width, `--ds-chart-height` tall. The row, label, track and segments are recharts nodes. (batch 4)
- `.ds-piechart, .ds-piechart__svg, .ds-piechart__slice` → `.ds-pie-chart-root` — Only the root survives (it centres the chart). The surface-coloured 1px seam between slices moved into chart.css, as `.ds-chart-container .recharts-sector[stroke="#fff"]` — recharts hard-codes a white hairline and the rule repaints it. (batch 4)
- `.ds-donut, .ds-donut__svg, .ds-donut__track, .ds-donut__segment, .ds-donut__center, .ds-donut__center-label` → `.ds-donut-chart-root, .ds-donut-chart-center-label, .ds-donut-chart-center-caption` — The ring itself is a recharts <Pie> now, so the track and the segments are gone. The two centre text classes survive under new names: `__center` (the figure) is `-center-label`, and `__center-label` (the caption under it) is `-center-caption` — the old pair read backwards. (batch 4)
- `.ds-gauge__svg, .ds-gauge__track, .ds-gauge__value, .ds-gauge__center, .ds-gauge__label` → `.ds-gauge-svg, .ds-gauge-track, .ds-gauge-value, .ds-gauge-center, .ds-gauge-label` — Flat-kebab rename, no structural change: the gauge stays library-free, so hand-written markup keeps working after a find-and-replace of `__` for `-`. `.ds-gauge` itself is unchanged, and the value arc's transition is now a CSS declaration rather than an inline style. (batch 4)
- `.ds-sparkline__svg, .ds-sparkline__line, .ds-sparkline__area, .ds-sparkline__dot` → `.ds-sparkline-svg, .ds-sparkline-line, .ds-sparkline-area, .ds-sparkline-dot` — Flat-kebab rename, no structural change; the sparkline stays library-free. `.ds-sparkline` keeps its `color: var(--ds-chart-1)` default, so an inline sparkline still paints from the series ramp rather than the accent. (batch 4)
- `.ds-sparkline--animate` → `.ds-sparkline-line--animate` — The modifier moved from the root onto the polyline, which is the element the keyframe draws. The keyframe and its reduced-motion opt-out stay in components/motion.css. (batch 4)
- `(none — height was a Tailwind class in the source)` → `--ds-chart-height` — The knob that replaced the source's `h-56`/`h-64`/`h-40`/`h-24` literals. `.ds-chart-container--plot` and `--square` read it, defaulting to 14rem and 16rem; set it on the chart to retune one. This package has no Tailwind and no tailwind-merge, so a competing height class would be decided by stylesheet order — a variable is not. (batch 4)
- `css/components/charts.css, css/components/bar-chart.css` → `css/components/chart.css, css/components/gauge.css, css/components/stacked-bar.css, css/components/pie-chart.css, css/components/donut-chart.css` — Anyone importing css/diametral.css is unaffected. A consumer cherry-picking the two old files has to swap them for the five new ones (and keep css/components/sparkline.css, which was already separate). (batch 4)
- `(none — the label and value column widths were Tailwind arbitrary-property classes in the source)` → `--ds-bullet-label, --ds-bullet-value` — The knobs that replaced the source's `[--bullet-label:7rem]` / `[--bullet-value:4rem]` literals on BulletChart's own className. `.ds-bullet-chart` declares both as its defaults and reads them in `grid-template-columns`; set either on the chart or on a wrapper to retune one bullet or a whole stack. Unprefixed `--bullet-*` is not read — every custom property in this package is `--ds-*`. (batch 5)
- `(none — net-new)` → `--ds-heat-1 … --ds-heat-5` — The sequential ramp `.ds-heatmap` quantises into, one hue getting darker. Separate from the categorical `--ds-chart-*` ramp on purpose: reading a categorical ramp as a scale is the classic dataviz error. It is also the one Tier-1 primitive css/themes/dark.css overrides — a sequential ramp encodes magnitude, so "more" has to mean brighter on a dark page. A theme that recolours data now has two ramps to consider, not one. (batch 5)
